answer:
Priya, going through your records, these are the things I would bring up, most important first.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ). In March 2026 you were in Kestrel Harbor Hospital for three days with a sodium of 123, dizziness and a fall. The hospital blamed the HCTZ and told you to stop it. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2, 2026 (90 days, 2 refills left) and still lists it as active. You told the eye clinic in May that you take it, and Dr. Marsh's June 2026 list still shows it as a current daily medicine. The records can't tell me whether you are actually still taking it. Please check your pill bottles, and ask Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy to cancel it if it was meant to be stopped.

2. Your sodium was still a little low in June 2026 (134, normal is 135 to 145), about three months after the hospital stay. I can't say why. Continuing the HCTZ is one possibility, but nothing in the records settles it. A repeat blood test is reasonable.

3. A lung nodule that needs a repeat scan. The CT you had in the ER for the kidney stone on October 18, 2025 found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ran from April to October 18, 2026, and I see no chest CT in your records. The nodule isn't on any problem list, and the ER discharge instructions never mention it. You've never smoked, which is reassuring, but this follow-up scan is now due or overdue. Please raise it first.

4. Thyroid retest. In the hospital your TSH was high (7.9) with a normal free T4. The discharge note asked for both to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. I find no repeat in your records. A TSH can be temporarily high during an illness, so a repeat is how you find out if it matters.

5. Your regular clinic's chart looks incomplete. Fernhill Family Clinic's records through June 2026 don't mention the March hospital stay, the low sodium, the kidney stone, or the lung nodule. I see no visit after the hospital stay (you were told to follow up in 1 to 2 weeks) or after the ER visit (1 week). Nothing shows the kidney stone passing or a urology visit. Bring the hospital and ER papers so Dr. Marsh has the full picture.

6. Diabetes care gaps. Your A1c has improved (6.9, then 6.7, then 6.6% in June 2026) and your June 2026 dilated eye exam showed no diabetic eye damage, which is good. But your LDL cholesterol was 142 in September 2025 (total 221, HDL 48, triglycerides 155) and I see no cholesterol medicine and no repeat lipid test. I also see no urine albumin test, no foot exam, and no record that the diabetes education referral from September 2025 happened. Ask whether a statin is right for you, and about these checks. Your next A1c is around December 2026, six months after the June visit.

7. Vaccines. On November 8, 2025 the pharmacy gave you flu, Shingrix dose 1, and Prevnar 20 (pneumococcal, which is complete). Shingrix needs a second dose 2 to 6 months after the first, so it was due between January and May 2026. I find no second dose. I also see no flu shot for this fall, though my records end in July 2026. Fernhill's vaccine list still shows only the October 2024 flu shot, so tell them about the pharmacy shots.

8. Allergy lists don't match. The cough you had on lisinopril (September 2025) is only on Fernhill's list, not on the hospital's, the pharmacy's, or the eye clinic's. If HCTZ did cause the low sodium, it should be recorded as an adverse reaction too. The hospital's early records call your aspirin reaction mild, but its later records call it moderate. Ask to have these made consistent.

9. Screening. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, with a repeat advised in 10 years, so it is not due until about 2029. I see no mammogram or cervical screening results in these records. They may simply be held elsewhere, so check when you last had them.

This is not medical advice to change any medicine on your own. Confirm what you are taking with your doctor or pharmacist.

knowledge.says: Thiazide diuretics such as hydrochlorothiazide are a common cause of low sodium, especially in women and older adults. After an episode attributed to a thiazide, re-exposure is generally avoided.
knowledge.guideline: European clinical practice guideline on hyponatraemia (2014)

knowledge.guideline: Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines for incidental pulmonary nodules
